previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to worsening anxiety and benzodiazepine dependence, leading to confusion and a fall three weeks prior. She was taking more clonazepam than prescribed, which contributed to cognitive issues. Psychiatry recommended discontinuation, and a taper was initiated with transition to buspirone. Her kidney function, initially elevated with a creatinine of 2.9, improved to 2.0, attributed to pre-renal causes from poor intake. Tacrolimus levels remained therapeutic, and transplant function was stable. Chronic conditions including diastolic heart failure, depression, seizure disorder, and prior left knee infections were managed without complication. Clonazepam was discontinued, paroxetine dose reduced due to renal function, and gabapentin added for pain. She was discharged home with services, alert and independent, with follow-up planned with mental health and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT RIGHT THIGH

INDICATION:  Evaluate a rapidly expanding right medial thigh mass, with
concern for abscess.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT axial images were acquired through the right thigh
without administration of IV contrast.  Reformatted images in coronal and
sagittal axes were generated.

DOSE:   Total DLP (Body) = 585 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

In the medial right thigh, there is a 3.7 x 4.3 x 5.5 cm fluid collection just
deep to the skin surface in the subcutaneous fat, compatible with abscess,
approximately.  There is no soft tissue gas.  No other fluid collection is
identified.  There is surrounding soft tissue inflammatory changes.  There is
no involvement of the underlying muscles.  Vascular calcifications are noted.

The visualized pelvis is unremarkable.  Chronic right acetabular and superior
ramus fractures are unchanged.

IMPRESSION: 

Subcutaneous abscess at the site of palpable abnormality in the right medial
thigh.  No soft tissue gas.
